chunks: And Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a borrowed item that a person borrows, and it then perishes or is stolen. So he said: “If he is trustworthy, then there is no liability upon him.”

key_terms.أَمِينًا: trustworthy; one who safeguards what is entrusted
key_terms.الْعَارِيَّةِ: a borrowed item given for temporary use
key_terms.فَتَهْلِكُ: then it perishes or is destroyed

ai.seo_question: Is a trustworthy borrower liable if a borrowed item is destroyed or stolen?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a borrowed item that is lost through destruction or theft. It states that when the borrower is trustworthy, he is not held financially liable for the loss, indicating that liability is not established merely by the occurrence of loss without breach of trust.
